question: Does my state tax my pension or my Social Security?

nuggets.text: At 65 or older (or totally disabled), pension income from an employer retirement system may be subtracted, up to a cap tied to the maximum Social Security benefit.
nuggets.quote: the cumulative or total annuity, pension, or endowment income from an employee retirement system included in federal adjusted gross income; or

nuggets.text: The cap is reduced by Social Security and Railroad Retirement benefits received.
nuggets.quote: less any payment received as old age, survivors, or disability benefits under the Social Security Act, the Railroad Retirement Act, or both.

nuggets.text: IRAs do not count as an employee retirement system.
nuggets.quote: an individual retirement account or annuity under § 408 of the Internal Revenue Code;

notes: Tax-General § 10-207 (the Social Security and military retirement subtractions) is not in this copy's Maryland index.
